Get free F1 betting tips and predictions from the OLBG tipster community, covering every qualifying session, sprint and Grand Prix, plus season-long ante-post markets. Our F1 Drivers' Championship and Constructors' Championship guides explain those markets in more detail.

NASCAR and IndyCar outright winner tips also appear here when available. If you'd rather follow the tipsters behind the tips, see our motor racing tipsters, or browse today's betting tips across 20 other sports.
F1 & Motor Racing Tips and Predictions at OLBG

The OLBG tipster community covers F1 race by race, with tips for qualifying, sprints and Grands Prix as well as season-long ante-post markets. NASCAR and IndyCar tips are less frequent and are limited to ante-post winner markets.

SeriesRaces in a seasonTips available

NASCAR Cup SeriesOver 30 racesAnte-post winner tips
IndyCar SeriesMore than 15 racesAnte-post winner tips

Tipsters can add comments to explain their selections, so you can read the reasoning behind each motor racing prediction before deciding whether to back it.

Most Popular F1 & Motor Racing Tips

The tips table at the top of this page lists upcoming races and season-long markets, ordered by the number of tips on each event's most popular selection. Beside each event, you will see that selection, along with the number and percentage of tips it has received.

Value Rating for Motor Racing Tips

The Value Rating shown beside the most popular tips compares the odds on offer for a selection with its theoretical chance of winning, based on the percentage of tips it has received. The higher the rating, the more value a selection may offer compared with its odds, up to a maximum of five stars. It is a guide to value rather than a guarantee of a winner.
How Can I See More Detail on F1 & Motor Racing Tips?

Click any event name in the tips table at the top of this page to open the full event page, which shows every market tipped for that event.

For each outcome, you will see how many OLBG tipsters have tipped it compared with the total number of tips on that market, giving you the percentage of support for that outcome.

At the top of each event page are two boxes. The Most Popular Pick is the outcome that has received the most tips for that event. The Best Tipster's Pick is the tip from the tipster with the highest profit who has tipped on the event.

Next to each tip, you can also see the tipster's annual profit and strike rate, their recent form and the reasoning in their comment, so you can judge the tip before deciding whether to back it.
How to Back F1 & Motor Racing Tips

Once you have found a tip you like, use the "Add" button to add it to your betslip. You can do this from this page or from any event page.

When your betslip is complete, you can compare the odds offered by different bookmakers. Choose a bookmaker and your betslip is transferred to their site, where you can place your bet.

A race can turn on a single safety car, a first-lap incident or a change in the weather, so set your limits before the race weekend and only bet what you can afford to lose. You must be 18 or over to bet. For free support and advice, visit GamCare or GambleAware, or read our responsible gambling guide.
F1 Betting Tips: Qualifying, Sprint & Race Predictions

OLBG tipsters cover the whole F1 season, from the opening round to the final Grand Prix. Every race weekend has F1 tips and predictions for pole position and the race, with the same markets tipped for the sprint on sprint weekends, plus ante-post markets throughout the season.

MarketWhat the tip covers
Fastest QualifierPole position: the driver who sets the fastest qualifying time (each-way available)
Win RaceRace winner: the driver who wins the race or sprint (each-way available)
Podium FinishA driver to finish in the top three
Top 6 FinishA driver to finish in the top six
Points FinishA driver to finish in a points-scoring position
Fastest LapThe driver who sets the quickest lap
Win TournamentAnte-post winner markets, such as the Drivers' Championship, including "Without" versions with a named favourite removed

Each-way terms vary between bookmakers, with two or three places typically paid, so check the terms before you place a bet. Tips usually appear two to three days before the race weekend. For the latest news and information on upcoming races, visit the official F1 website.

Open any tip to read the tipster's comment and see their F1 tipping record. To compare tipsters rather than tips, see our best motor racing tipsters.

F1 Sprint Race Betting Tips & Predictions

On a sprint weekend, there are two qualifying sessions and two races, which means two sets of F1 tips and predictions to follow. Sprint weekends are marked "Yes" in the Sprint column of the F1 calendar above.

How an F1 Sprint Weekend Works

A sprint weekend replaces the usual second and third practice sessions with Sprint Qualifying (sometimes called the Sprint Shootout) and the sprint race.

DayStandard weekendSprint weekend
FridayPractice 1 and Practice 2Practice 1 and Sprint Qualifying
SaturdayPractice 3 and QualifyingSprint race and Qualifying
SundayGrand PrixGrand Prix

Sprint Qualifying sets the grid for the sprint, while Saturday's Qualifying sets the grid for the Grand Prix. The sprint result does not decide who starts on pole on Sunday.

Sprint Race Markets We Tip

Our tipsters cover the same markets for the sprint as for the Grand Prix: Fastest Qualifier, Win Race, Podium Finish, Top 6 Finish, Points Finish and Fastest Lap. Each-way terms can apply to the Fastest Qualifier and Win Race markets, and they vary between bookmakers.

Check the points rules before backing a Points Finish tip. Only the top eight score in a sprint, compared with the top ten in a Grand Prix.

What Changes Between a Sprint and a Grand Prix

A sprint is around 100 km, roughly a third of a Grand Prix distance, and typically lasts about 30 minutes. That leaves less time to recover from a poor start or an incident, and fewer points are on offer, with 8 for the winner down to 1 for eighth.

Because each race has its own qualifying session, a driver's sprint form and Grand Prix form can differ. Our tipsters explain their reasoning in the comments on each event page.
F1 Betting Stats: How Starting Position Affects Race Results

We have analysed every Grand Prix and sprint race from 2021 to 2025, which is 114 Grand Prix races and 24 sprint races. The tables show how often drivers won, finished on the podium, finished in the top six or scored points from each starting position. They relate directly to our Win Race, Podium Finish, Top 6 Finish and Points Finish markets.

The driver starting from P1 won 55% of Grands Prix, and 75% of winners started from the front row. Winning from the back is rare but not impossible, as two Grands Prix were won from P11 or lower, from 14th and 17th on the grid. Reliability still matters: around one in ten starters retired from a Grand Prix.

The Fastest Lap market is far more open than the winner market, as a driver outside the top ten took it in around one Grand Prix in eight. The Grand Prix figures cover 113 races, as no fastest lap was recognised at the 2021 Belgian Grand Prix.

Starting position is the grid slot after any penalties. The tables exclude pit-lane starts and drivers who did not start, which is why P1 and P2 each show one fewer starter than there were starters in the Grand Prix.
F1 Race Predictions: What Affects the Result

An F1 race prediction rarely rests on car speed alone. These are the main factors to weigh when you read tips and comments for a qualifying session, sprint or Grand Prix.

Qualifying and Starting Position

Where a driver starts shapes almost every race market. In our stats for the last five completed seasons, three-quarters of Grand Prix winners started from the front row. Check whether a driver's grid slot reflects their qualifying pace or a penalty, because a driver who starts further back than their pace deserves can often recover places, especially where overtaking is easier.

Circuit Layout and Overtaking

Some circuits make passing difficult, which puts extra weight on qualifying and the Fastest Qualifier market. Monaco is the classic example. Circuits with long straights and several overtaking zones give drivers a better chance of recovering from a poor qualifying session, which can open up the Podium Finish, Top 6 Finish and Points Finish markets.

Weather and Tyre Strategy

Rain can scramble both qualifying and the race, and changeable conditions make tyre choice and pit-stop timing more important. In dry races, circuits that are hard on tyres put extra emphasis on strategy, so a driver who manages their tyres well can beat a quicker rival. Check the forecast before you back a selection.

Safety Cars, Virtual Safety Cars and Reliability

A safety car or Virtual Safety Car (VSC) slows the field, which makes a pit stop cheaper for drivers who stop under it. Timing matters: a leader who has not pitted before the VSC ends can find that rivals behind have already stopped cheaply. The leader then has to pit under normal racing conditions and loses more time, which can cost places. Safety cars can also bunch up the field and reshuffle the order, and they are more common at street circuits.

Reliability matters too: around one in ten Grand Prix starters in our data retired, so even strong favourites can fail to finish.

About This F1 & Motor Racing Tips Page

The tips on this page come from OLBG's tipsters, whose results are shown beside every tip. The page itself is edited by Andy Powell, who has been an OLBG member since 2005 and has worked for OLBG since 2015. He wrote our five motor racing preview guides and writes the content on our Grand Prix event pages.

About the editor

Andy has followed F1 for over 20 years and watches every qualifying session, sprint and Grand Prix live, whatever the time zone. He compiled the results database behind the F1 stats on this page and, as editor, keeps the page current through the season, while the tips themselves come from OLBG's tipsters.

- Andy Powell, Content Editor
